setlist.title: It Must Have Been The Roses

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): The transition into Fire On The Mountain is spectacular, with Jerry taking off dramatically; Reviewer hears three false climaxes before a ripping Jerry jam peaks into Fire; calls it the best Scarlet>Fire ever [12][17]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): Bobby plays slide, then Brent solos, then Bobby and Jerry tear it down [18]
- **Lost Sailor** (1 review): Lost Sailor into Saint of Circumstance into an epic Deal is praised [19]
- **Deal** (1 review): Deal is described as a flaming meteor of energy [18]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (1 review): Jerry's playing in Fire is called unfocused and limp, though the Scarlet transition is a highlight [20]
- **Playin' In The Band** (1 review): Playin' is called excellent, with guitar reminiscent of Warren Haynes [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-11-30.110936.mtx.chappell.sb31.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 197 min; rated 4.25/5 by 12 [1]. Said about its sound: Digital static was removed from the first seconds of Stranger by Mike Parillo [1]
- **gd1980-11-30.157922.aud.hicks-fong.flac2448**: audience recording; 24 songs; 193 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd80-11-30.sbd-aud.sacks.2416.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 182 min; rated 4.43/5 by 58 [4]. Said about its sound: Recording is intelligently edited, well-blended and smooth; Soundboard sounds exceptionally good, rare for this era; Sound quality is good [11][13][20]
- **gd1980-11-30.part.127319.aud.oade.stankiewicz.wise.minches.flac24**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 159 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [5]. Said about its sound: Teac mics sound nice, and the mix by Dan Healy sounds pretty good [5]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says Jerry played strongly from the opening and the band was clean that night [15]
- Reviewer says the band always seemed to make magic at the Fox [16]
- Jerry gets the lyrics right on nearly every song; Loser struggled a bit [18]
- Reviewer calls the second set a remarkable journey, played with fire throughout [22]
- Tapers got busted at the start of Ramble On Rose and were offline for a while [2]
- Security was difficult, the mic stand was head level, and there is some chatter [5]
- Finds the first set weak, like a night off, compared with the excellent second set [17]
- Placed among the first newer electric shows after Radio City and Warfield runs [19]
- Recommends the 10-10-80 show for a hotter Scarlet>Fire [20]
- Heads disagree on Scarlet/Fire; some call it the best ever, others overrated [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-11-30.110936.mtx.chappell.sb31.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by Chris Chappell; source: Matrix (SBD/AUD mix) Ratio ~ Phi [1]. Also: Taped by Dr. Bob Wagner on Nakamichi 700s with bass EQ to cassette master; transferred and mastered by Chris Chappell; Matrix combines AUD1 (24-bit set 1), AUD2 for Scarlet>Fire, and AUD3 for the rest [1]
- **gd1980-11-30.157922.aud.hicks-fong.flac2448**: taped by concert recording by John Hicks & Dennis Fong; transferred by Transferred by Andrew F. 09/2022; source: Unknown mics & deck > Sony Fe-Cr 90's [2]. Also: Other sources patch Ramble On Rose through Big River, and tape flips in Saint and Drums [2]
- **gd80-11-30.sbd-aud.sacks.2416.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard and Audience composite [4]
- **gd1980-11-30.part.127319.aud.oade.stankiewicz.wise.minches.flac24**: taped by Jim Oade; Richie Stankiewicz; Jim Wise; transferred by David Minches; source: Set 1 - Master Audience Cassette: 2 Teac ME-120s> Sony D-5 location SBD; Set 2 - Master Audience Cassette: 2 Beyer M160s> Sony D-5 location SBD [5]. Also: Recorded by Jim Oade and Jim Wise with Teac ME-120 mics and a JVC KD2 cassette recorder; untransferred for 33 years [5]
